audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 20, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal military-history and witness audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for siege, wives and children as demanded property, palace search, intoxication context, youth deployment, mass casualties, hill/valley religious stereotyping, wall collapse, prisoner negotiation, royal mercy, treaty, coerced prophetic injury, lion death, disguise, herem language, and condemnation of released captive.

verses.restored: Ben-hadad king of Aram gathered all his army; thirty-two kings were with him, with horses and chariots. He went up, besieged Samaria, and fought against it.
He sent messengers into city to Ahab king of Israel and said to him, Thus says Ben-hadad:
Your silver and gold are mine; your wives and your children, the best, are mine.
King of Israel answered, According to your word, my lord the king, I am yours and all I have.
Messengers returned and said, Thus says Ben-hadad: Though I sent to you, saying, Give me your silver, gold, wives, and children,
tomorrow at this time I will send my servants to search your house and houses of your servants. Everything desirable in your eyes they shall place in their hands and take.
King of Israel called all elders of land and said, Please know and see this one seeks evil. He sent for my wives, children, silver, and gold, and I did not withhold from him.
All elders and all people said to him, Do not listen and do not consent.
He said to messengers of Ben-hadad, Say to my lord the king: All you sent to your servant at first I will do, but this matter I cannot do. Messengers went and returned word.
Ben-hadad sent to him: Thus may gods do to me and thus add, if dust of Samaria is enough for handfuls for all people at my feet.
King of Israel answered, Speak: Let one girding on armor not boast like one taking it off.
When Ben-hadad heard this word, he and kings were drinking in shelters. He said to servants, Set yourselves. They set themselves against city.
Look, a prophet came near Ahab king of Israel and said, Thus says YHWH: Have you seen all this great multitude? Look, I am giving it into your hand this day, and you shall know I am YHWH.
Ahab said, By whom? He said, Thus says YHWH: By young men of provincial officials. He said, Who shall begin battle? He said, You.
He counted young men of provincial officials, two hundred thirty-two. After them he counted all people, all children of Israel, seven thousand.
They went out at noon while Ben-hadad was drinking himself drunk in shelters, he and thirty-two kings helping him.
Young men of provincial officials went out first. Ben-hadad sent, and they told him, Men came out from Samaria.
He said, If for peace they came, seize them alive; if for battle they came, seize them alive.
These young men of provincial officials went out from city, and army followed them.
Each struck his man. Arameans fled, and Israel pursued them. Ben-hadad king of Aram escaped upon horse with horsemen.
King of Israel went out, struck horses and chariots, and struck Aram with a great blow/slaughter.
The prophet came near king of Israel and said, Go, strengthen yourself, know and see what you shall do, for at turn of year king of Aram will come up against you.
Servants of king of Aram said, Their gods are gods of mountains; therefore they were stronger than we. But let us fight them in plain; surely we shall be stronger.
Do this matter: remove kings each from his place and put governors in their places.
Count for yourself an army like army that fell from you, horse for horse and chariot for chariot. We will fight them in plain; surely we shall be stronger. He listened to their voice and did so.
At turn of year Ben-hadad counted Arameans and went up to Aphek to fight Israel.
Children of Israel were counted, provisioned, and went to meet them. Children of Israel camped before them like two little flocks of goats, while Arameans filled land.

Man of Divine came near and spoke to king of Israel: Thus says YHWH: Because Arameans said YHWH is Divine of mountains and not Divine of valleys, I will give all this great multitude into your hand, and you shall know I am YHWH.
They camped opposite each other seven days. On seventh day battle joined. Children of Israel struck one hundred thousand Aramean foot soldiers in one day.
The remaining fled to Aphek, into city, and wall fell upon twenty-seven thousand remaining people. Ben-hadad fled and came into city, into inner chamber.

His servants said, Look, we heard kings of house of Israel are kings of covenant-kindness. Please let us place sackcloth upon waists and ropes upon heads and go to king of Israel; perhaps he will preserve your life.
They girded sackcloth upon waists, ropes upon heads, came to king of Israel, and said, Your servant Ben-hadad says, Please let me live. Ahab said, Is he still alive? He is my brother.
The men took it as omen and hurried to confirm word from him, saying, Your brother Ben-hadad. He said, Go, bring him. Ben-hadad came out to him, and Ahab brought him up into chariot.

Ben-hadad said, Cities my father took from your father I will restore, and you may establish streets/markets for yourself in Damascus as my father did in Samaria. Ahab said, I will send you away with this covenant. He cut covenant with him and sent him away.
A certain man from sons of prophets said to his companion by word of YHWH, Please strike me. The man refused to strike him.
He said, Because you did not listen to voice of YHWH, look, when you go from me a lion shall strike you. He went from him, and lion found him and struck/killed him.
He found another man and said, Please strike me. The man struck him, striking and wounding him.
The prophet went and waited for king by road, disguising himself with bandage/covering over his eyes.

As king passed, he cried to king: Your servant went into midst of battle, and look, a man turned aside and brought a man to me, saying, Guard this man. If missing, your life shall be in place of his life, or you shall weigh a talent of silver.
While your servant was doing here and there, he was gone. King of Israel said to him, Thus is your judgment; you yourself decided it.
He hurried and removed covering from his eyes, and king of Israel recognized him as one of prophets.
He said to him, Thus says YHWH: Because you sent from your hand a man I devoted to destruction, your life shall be in place of his life and your people in place of his people.
King of Israel went to his house sullen and angry and came to Samaria.

translation_notes: Ben-hadad treats silver, gold, wives, and children as possessions transferable from one king to another. Women and children are hostages and persons, never royal property.
Ahab initially agrees to surrender his household and wealth before resisting the invasive search. His eventual boundary does not erase his willingness to assign other people's lives.
Ben-hadad's intoxication occurs during military command, but alcohol should not become an ethnic or moral stereotype or excuse for Israel's slaughter.
Young provincial attendants lead the attack. Youth language must not romanticize child soldiers or pressure inexperienced people into combat.

The reported one hundred thousand deaths and wall killing twenty-seven thousand require textual, rhetorical, and historical audit; ancient battle numbers may be hyperbolic and must not become celebratory statistics.
Aramean claims about mountain and valley gods are wartime religious interpretation. They do not justify contempt toward Arameans or other religions.

Ben-hadad negotiates survival, restoration of cities, and trade rights. Mercy toward a captive is not inherently sinful, even though political accountability and protection of victims remain necessary.

A prophet orders a companion to strike him; refusal is followed by death from a lion. This sacred-violence story must not be used to coerce assault, punish conscientious refusal, or treat animals as execution tools.
The final oracle uses herem—devotion to destruction—to condemn Ahab for releasing Ben-hadad. It must not teach that mercy is disobedience or that captives should be executed.
Ahab's covenant with Ben-hadad may be politically self-serving, but ethical critique should focus on justice, restitution, and future safety rather than demanding killing.
safety_note: Do not treat wives, children, captives, or cities as royal property. Do not glorify casualty totals, coerce someone to strike another person, or teach that mercy deserves punishment. Reject herem as a modern policy; pursue accountable peace, restitution, due process, and protection of civilians.
